newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares end up, downside seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up, downside seen limited.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index closed slightly higher on Tuesday, with technical charts showing the market had limited downside at current levels, brokers said.
The index edged up 0.56 point or 0.43 percent to 131.45 on turnover of HK$34 million against Monday's HK$45 million.
The domestic A share index lost 0.76 point or 0.18 percent to 413.23 on turnover of 4.1 billion yuan against 5.2 billion in the previous session.
"Technically speaking, the B share index seems to have bottomed out," an analyst at Everbright Securities said.
Further advances in television tube maker Shenzhen SEG helped to buoy the B share index, the Everbright analyst said.

SEG, the best B share performer, soared HK$0.41 or 7.75 percent to HK$5.70 on volume of 1.3 million shares. It was the day's second most actively traded issue. Analysts said SEG was targeted by some foreign institutional bargain hunters after recent losses.
Analysts also said the overall B share market lacked buying interest as well as market-moving news.
"B share trading is still very inactive," an analyst at China Southern Securities said. "The market is expected to remain quiet in the near future."
Bengang Steel Plates 2761.SZ was the most actively traded B share issue on volume of 2.0 million shares, falling HK$0.01 to HK$2.12 against a recent offer price of HK$2.38 per share.
On the A share market, Emeishan Salt was the biggest loser, sliding 0.20 yuan or 4.42 percent to 4.32 yuan on volume of 2.4 million shares.
Analysts said they expected the A share market consolidation to extend into later this week.
